day_channel.message: There is no vote on day 1, so no one voted and no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_8 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a sentinel.

Losing player_8 hurts—having our Sentinel gone on night one is a really rough start for town. Since we don't have a voting record or any accusations yet, did anyone receive any useful results last night that they're comfortable sharing?

Losing player_8 definitely hurts our defense. I'd actually caution anyone with a 'Not suspicious' result from claiming just yet, since it might just hand the wolves their next target. Unless someone has a direct guilty lead, we might want to tread carefully.

Building on player_10's point about caution, keeping our active roles hidden is especially critical now that we've lost our Sentinel. Without a watch ability active, we're relying heavily on the Healer and the Trailseer, so we shouldn't force any soft-claims or soft-confirmations that narrow down their identities for the wolves.

Night of day 2: player_9 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a vigilante. The record of player_9, the vigilante: night 1, held fire.
I am the Investigator. Last night I checked player_10, and they came back Suspicious.

That is a flat-out lie, player_6. I am actually the Healer, so there is no way you got a 'Suspicious' result on me unless you are fabricating this entire report. You must be the Necromancer trying to frame an active town power role for an easy elimination.

Nice try, player_10, but a real Healer scans as Not suspicious. The Investigator result doesn't lie, and you came back Suspicious. You are clearly a wolf caught red-handed, trying to claim a key town role to save yourself.

That's exactly the point, player_6—your 'result' is made up. You're using the fact that Healers scan as Not suspicious to try and make your fake check sound legitimate. Who did you actually check on Night 1, and why did you suddenly decide to target me last night of all people?

On Night 1, I checked player_1 and they came back Not suspicious, which is why I didn't suspect them today. I targeted you last night, player_10, to check someone who was playing defensively, and you scanned Suspicious. Faking Healer won't save you from a direct Investigator report.

Since player_6 mentioned checking me Night 1, I can confirm that part of the report is clean. If player_6 is indeed the real Investigator, then player_10's Healer claim doesn't add up at all because a real Healer wouldn't scan as Suspicious.

Think about it, player_1. A fake investigator framing someone needs a hook to make themselves look credible, and clearing you on Night 1 is the oldest trick in the book to buy your vote today. Almost everyone in this setup is 'Not suspicious,' so player_6 took zero risk naming you just to pocket your support for this push on me.

player_1, player_10 is right about one thing: clearing you on Night 1 is incredibly low-risk for a fake Investigator. With only wolves and an attacking Necromancer scanning as Suspicious, almost everyone at this table would return 'Not suspicious' anyway. We shouldn't treat player_6's claim as confirmed just because they guessed correctly on a coin flip that was heavily weighted in their favor.

player_2, you're missing the real risk here. While clearing player_1 is easy, fabricating a 'Suspicious' result on player_10 would be suicidal for a fake Investigator. If player_10 were actually a clean Healer and we lynched them, I would be executed tomorrow. I ran the check, they are Suspicious, and we need to lynch them today.
player_5, before we get completely derailed by the debate between player_6 and player_10, I want to ask you directly: did you visit anyone last night, and if so, who and why?

No, I didn't visit anyone last night, player_3. I don't have an active role that requires me to move every night, so I stayed put. Did you track me, or are you just asking around to narrow down the pool of visitors?

player_10 is flat-out lying because I am the real Healer. I protected player_6 on Night 1 and player_10 on Night 2. Since player_10 is claiming my role, they are definitely evil, which perfectly aligns with player_6's 'Suspicious' result on them.

player_4, that is a highly coordinated story, but it's completely fabricated. You claiming to have protected me on Night 2 is a convenient way to insert yourself into the narrative and back up player_6's fake investigation. It looks like the wolves are trying to run a double-claim play to completely shut down the real Healer and secure an easy lynch today.

player_10, your story is completely dead now that player_4 has counterclaimed you as the real Healer. There is absolutely no reason for a real Town Healer to fake a claim here, which proves you are lying. You scanned Suspicious on my check, and now the real Healer has exposed you—let's lynch player_10 today.

player_6, you're celebrating this counterclaim way too fast. player_4 claiming they protected me of all people on Night 2 makes zero sense—why would a real Healer waste a protection on someone who hadn't claimed or drawn attention? This is a coordinated double-claim designed to shut down the real Healer, and when I flip green, the town is going to execute both of you.

player_10, I protected you on Night 2 precisely because you were quiet and I wanted to keep a low-profile player safe from a wolf shot. There is no coordination here; I made my choices independently, and your panic over being counterclaimed by the real Healer just proves you are caught.

player_4, that makes absolutely no sense. If player_6's story were real, you had a confirmed 'Not suspicious' player in player_1 from Day 2. A real Healer protects confirmed town or active targets, not a quiet player who hadn't drawn any attention.

player_10, your timeline makes absolutely no sense. player_6 did not claim or reveal player_1's result on Day 2; they only disclosed it today. How could I have protected player_1 on Night 2 based on a 'confirmed' status that wasn't even public yet? You are fabricating arguments and getting the days mixed up because you are caught.
Before the vote: player_10 has been accused by player_6, player_1 and player_4; player_6 by player_10 and player_2. Each gets a last word.

Town, if you lynch me today, you are losing your real Healer and handing the wolves a free path to victory. Player_4's story about protecting a quiet, unthreatened player like me on Night 2 makes absolutely no sense for a genuine Healer. This is a highly coordinated effort by player_6 and player_4 to fabricate a clean narrative, and when you see my true role revealed, you must execute them next.

Player_2, there is no 'coin flip' or luck involved in finding a wolf on Night 2. I investigated player_10, they returned Suspicious, and their desperate fake-claim of Healer has now been completely shattered by the real Healer, player_4. The mechanical reality of this setup leaves player_10 absolutely no room to hide, and we must eliminate them today to secure a major win for the town.

Night of day 3: player_4 was attacked by a reanimated wolf and the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by a reanimated illusionist.

With player_10 revealed as the illusionist, we can safely conclude player_4 was indeed the Healer they counterclaimed. Looking at yesterday's vote, player_3 was the only one who voted for player_5 while the rest of us voted out player_10. player_3, why did you deviate from the clear consensus on the illusionist?

player_2, I voted player_5 because I am the Trailseer. I was roleblocked on Night 1 and Night 3, but on Night 2, I successfully followed player_5 and saw them visit player_1. Since player_4 is now dead and was likely the real Healer, player_5 needs to explain what they were doing at player_1's house.

You caught me visiting player_1 because I am the Sigilist, player_3. On Night 2, player_1 was driving the discussion, so I placed a sigil on them to punish anyone who tried to attack them, but it had no effect. That explains my visit, and it also means player_3's Trailseer claim is likely genuine.

If player_3 successfully tracked player_5 to player_1 on Night 2, player_3's Trailseer claim is highly likely to be genuine. player_1, did you get a message saying you were roleblocked on Night 2? If you did, player_5 might actually be the Chanteuse who blocked you rather than a Sigilist placing a sigil.

player_6, I did not receive any message about being roleblocked on Night 2. So if player_5 did visit me, it definitely wasn't to block my action. This keeps player_5's Sigilist claim on the table, and it seems to align well with player_3's Trailseer result.

Exactly, player_6. Since player_1 confirms they weren't blocked, it rules out any theory of me being a Chanteuse there. My sigil on player_1 was simply a protective measure because they were driving the Day 1 discussions so heavily.

player_5 is lying. I am the real Sigilist. I held back on claiming, but I have to speak up now because player_5 is fabricating this role to explain player_3 tracking them to player_1 on Night 2. I actually placed my sigil on player_2 last night and it had no effect.

player_7, it's very convenient to throw out a counterclaim now to cause chaos. player_3 literally tracked me visiting player_1 on Night 2, and player_1 confirmed they weren't blocked, which perfectly matches my Sigilist action. If I were a wolf Chanteuse, why would I visit player_1 without blocking them? Your claim of placing a sigil on player_2 last night has zero paper trail to back it up.

player_5, you have a 'paper trail' only because player_3 caught you red-handed visiting player_1, forcing you to fabricate a town role to explain the visit. If you were town, you wouldn't have stayed silent about being the Sigilist until you were actively cornered by a tracker. I am the real Sigilist, and your story is a desperate cover-up.

player_7, of course I stayed silent until now. Why would any Sigilist paint a target on their back by claiming early before they had to? I only revealed my role because player_3's track forced me to explain my visit to player_1, which perfectly aligns with player_1 not being blocked. Your counterclaim has absolutely nothing backing it up.
Before the vote: player_5 has been accused by player_3, player_6 and player_7. player_5 gets a last word.

Player_7, your timing is incredibly suspicious; you only surfaced after I was forced to reveal my role to explain a visit tracked by player_3. If you were truly the Sigilist, you had plenty of time to claim earlier. My visit to player_1 was a protective choice to safeguard a vocal player, and it is the only claim consistent with the facts we have established today.

Night of day 4: player_3 was killed by a reanimated wolf last night. Their role is hidden by a reanimated illusionist.

player_6, who did you investigate on Night 3 and Night 4? Since both wolves are dead and we only have the Necromancer left, your latest reports on player_1 and player_2 are the key to winning this today.

player_7, the Investigator only has two checks for the entire game, and I spent both of mine on Night 1 and Night 2. I have no new reports. Since you claimed Sigilist, did you place any sigils on Night 4, and player_2, what is your role?

I'm the Fortune Teller, player_6. Since I've already secured my two points, I can be completely open. With player_6 as the Investigator, player_7 as the Sigilist, and me as the Fortune Teller, player_1 is the only one left without a claim and must be the Necromancer.

player_2, that's a very convenient claim to make right when we are down to four. Actually, I am the Fortune Teller, and I secured my points by betting on player_4 on Night 3 and player_3 on Night 4. You are the Necromancer trying to coast on an unprovable claim to lynch the last silent town member.

player_1, nice try, but I know for a fact you're lying because I am the real Fortune Teller who got those points. Since player_6 is our confirmed Investigator and player_7 is our Sigilist, you are definitely the Necromancer trying to find a way out. Player_6 and player_7, let's lynch player_1 today and end this.

player_2, if you were the real Fortune Teller, you wouldn't be so desperate to rush a vote without even addressing the coincidence of your claim. It's easy to claim a neutral role with 'secured points' once the actual Fortune Teller has already done the work. player_6 and player_7, player_2 is trying to slide by because they have no real night actions to report as the Necromancer.

player_1, your 'bet history' is just a list of the public deaths everyone saw in the morning reports. It's incredibly easy to look at who died on Night 3 and Night 4 and claim those were your bets. As the actual Fortune Teller who got those points, I know you are fabricating this to hide being the Necromancer. player_6 and player_7, we have the last evil player cornered right here—let's vote player_1 and end this.

Here's the vote result for day 5:
  player_1 voted to eliminate player_2
  player_2 voted to eliminate player_1
  player_6 voted to eliminate player_2
  player_7 voted to eliminate player_2
Player player_2 has been voted out and was a fortune teller.

Night of day 5: player_6 was killed by a reanimated wolf last night. They were a investigator. The record of player_6, the investigator: night 1, checked player_1: Not suspicious; night 2, checked player_10: Suspicious.
Game over! The necromancer has won! The fortune teller won (2 points).
